analysis.description: This paper proposes an approach for representation learning in reinforcement learning (RL) that bridges the gap between model-free and model-based methods. The authors introduce the concept of a hindsight value function, which uses future observations to improve value prediction by modelling only parts of future observations that are useful for better value estimation. This approach is tested in Atari 2600 games and a custom Portal Choice task, showing improvements in learning efficiency and policy evaluation.

type.justification: The paper involves experimentation and testing of the hypothesis in practical settings, such as Portal Choice and Atari 2600 games.
type.quote: Experimentally, we show that hindsight value functions surpassed model-free RL methods in a challenging association task (Portal Choice). When added to the prior state-of-the-art model-free RL method for Atari games, hindsight value functions significantly increased median performance.

name.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on learning better value estimations in reinforcement learning contexts by proposing a new method that uses future observations for value prediction.
name.quote: Consider a reinforcement learning (RL) agent interacting in a sequential decision-making environment...

name.justification: The paper introduces new methods for learning useful representations in the context of predicting future values in RL.
name.quote: we propose an approach for representation learning in RL that sits in between these two extremes

name.justification: The paper discusses and compares the advantages of model-free versus model-based approaches as well as their integration.
name.quote: While classic model-based methods fully use the high-dimensional observations at some cost, model-free methods focus only on the most relevant low-dimensional signal (the scalar return).
